Locking and lifetime rules for program, map, socket, device, and firmware structures outside the migration and RCU scopes shown.

findings.text: Exposes a compile-time helper that yields the size of a named member within a named type by forming a member access through a null pointer. Callers use it for static size checks without instantiating the type.

Preserves caller-visible packet metadata pointers across program execution by saving the stored meta and end markers, recomputing data pointers for the run, invoking the program, then restoring the saved markers before returning the program result.

Defines matched save and restore handling for the packet data end marker, where saving captures the current marker and points it at the end of linear packet data, and restoring writes back a previously saved marker.

Provides access to packet control scratch storage mapped to queueing metadata, with compile-time assertions that the user-visible control area length matches the internal scratch length and the expected control length. Callers must clear this area when exposing it after unprivileged use to avoid leaking prior contents.

Conditionally protects packet control scratch around program execution when the program declares control access, by saving and clearing before the run and restoring afterward in the saving variant, or by clearing before a pinned run in the clearing variant. The saving wrapper disables migration around the inner run.

Requires migration to remain disabled across control-save program runs and across socket-lookup array walks, with each disable matched by a later enable on the same path, preventing CPU movement while per-CPU redirect or program state is in use.

Computes program memory footprints from instruction counts and structure layout, where instruction bytes scale with the stored length and total allocation covers at least the base program structure extended to the instruction array. Classic program length scales with the filter count in the same manner.
Identifies migrated classic programs by an unspecified program type, and normalizes context access sizes that exceed the machine word and divide evenly by it down to the machine word size.

Constrains narrow context loads to sizes within the default width that are powers of the radix, with the effective offset derived from the trailing bits of the requested offset in an endian-aware manner, while wide accesses require full wide integer size, containment within the target field, and natural alignment.

Enforces read-only protection for program images and JIT binaries after a flush-reset of permissions, where program locking is skipped when the image is already JITed or when always-on JIT mode applies, and binary locking upgrades to read-execute by applying read protection then execute permission.

Exposes socket filter entry points that trim packet capacity and report filtering outcome, with the plain variant mapping any drop reason to a permission failure and the reason variant returning the underlying drop reason directly.
Declares callback types for classic filter validation against socket filter arrays and for filling JIT image holes over a memory area with a given length.

Routes program release through a common free path, where the unlock-free wrapper delegates directly and the JIT free wrapper reuses the same path, while the release-other helper performs no action in the routed fragment.
Gates raw program dumps on the same visibility rule that governs symbol value display, denying dumps whenever symbol values would be hidden.
Reports unsupported operation for instruction patching and for JIT poke descriptor registration in the routed configuration, signalling callers to avoid these paths or handle failure.
Tracks a no-direct-return flag in per-CPU redirect state with query, set, and clear operations, where set asserts the flag, clear deasserts it, and query reports its current value.

Validates forward devices by requiring the interface to be up and the packet length to fit within the device MTU plus link header and VLAN overhead, returning distinct errors for down devices versus oversize packets.
Yields no socket in the routed reuseport run helper, indicating an unimplemented or disabled selection path that callers must treat as absence of selection.
Treats program symbol state as off when its list linkage is empty or points at the poison marker, indicating absence from the symbol table.

In the enabled JIT configuration, blinding is needed when requested but not yet applied, JIT availability follows build support and global enablement, JITed status follows per-program JIT state, blinding enablement additionally requires JIT request and hardening policy with an exemption for token holders bearing CAP_BPF at a specific hardening level, and symbol enablement requires hardening to be off and symbol support to be on at a specific level. Dumping emits diagnostics and a hex image when present.

In the disabled JIT and symbol configuration, enablement queries uniformly report negative, address lookup reports absence, text testing reports negative, symbol value query reports ERANGE, program lookup reports null, add and delete helpers perform no action, blinding need reports negative, and constant blinding returns its input unchanged.

Reserves BPF_ANC as a high flag bit in classic filter codes to tag ancillary loads, with a mapping macro that converts socket-filter ancillary offsets into tagged codes for protocol, type, index, attributes, marks, queueing, hardware, hash, CPU, ALU, VLAN, offset, and randomness sources.

Decides accumulator clearing from the leading classic instruction, preserving it only for immediate returns, length loads, and most absolute loads except the SKF_AD_ALU_XOR_X ancillary case, and translates absolute loads with ancillary offsets into tagged codes while asserting inputs are untagged and passing through other codes unchanged.
Reports the maximum ancillary identifier as the extent of supported classic extensions.
Lays out socket-address kernel context as socket pointer, address pointer, u64 temporary register for indirect stores, type-specific context pointer, and u32 address length.

Lays out socket-operations kernel context with a socket pointer, a union of fixed-length argument arrays and reply scalars typed u32, SYN and packet pointers with a data-end pointer, operation and state narrow fields typed u8, and a u64 scratch field marking the start of uninitialized tail storage that must precede any cleared additions.

Lays out sysctl kernel context with header and table pointers, current and new value pointers with size_t lengths, update and write flags, a file position pointer, and a u64 temporary for indirect stores.
Fixes the kernel sockopt staging buffer length as a small constant used to size inline byte storage for option handling.
Lays out sockopt staging storage as a byte array sized by the sockopt buffer constant.
Lays out sockopt kernel context with a socket pointer, option value range pointers typed u8, level name and length fields typed s32, a current task pointer for return values, and a u64 temporary.

Lays out socket-lookup kernel context with family and protocol typed u16, ports with network-order source and host-order destination, address storage as embedded storage or referenced storage for the respective families, a selected socket pointer, an ingress interface index typed u32, and a reuseport bypass flag.

Iterates the socket-lookup program array under migration disable, restoring the most recent selection before each program, updating the remembered socket and bypass flag on pass with selection, clearing the all-pass marker on the leading drop, and finally reporting pass when all passed or a socket was selected, else drop.
Holds RCU read protection across dereference and use of the network-namespace lookup array in the address-family helpers, releasing protection after the output socket pointer is assigned.

Exposes address-family lookup runners that build kernel context from supplied addresses, ports, protocol, and interface, invoke the shared array runner when present, and translate drop into ECONNREFUSED while returning the bypass flag.

Validates redirect flags against the allowed action set plus a caller mask, aborting on stray bits, then looks up the target; on miss without broadcast it clears map state to INT_MAX identity and BPF_MAP_TYPE_UNSPEC type and returns the embedded action, otherwise it records target index, map identity and type, storing the map and flags for broadcast or clearing them for direct mode before returning redirect.

Reports EOPNOTSUPP, null, no-op, or error-pointer behavior for packet byte load, store, pointer, copy, and metadata helpers in the routed configuration, indicating these paths require external support or must be avoided.
Declares _FIPS_H include guard with fips_enabled denoting off and fips_fail_notify performing no action.
Declares _LINUX_FIRMWARE_MAP_H and _LINUX_FIRMWARE_H as include guards.
Treats firmware map add and remove as always-successful no-ops in the routed configuration, and builtin firmware requests as always absent.
Defines FW_ACTION_NOUEVENT and FW_ACTION_UEVENT distinguishing no-event from uevent handling, ordered with no-event before uevent.
Lays out firmware blobs with size_t length, read-only data pointer, and private loader handle.
Enumerates firmware upload outcomes from success through hardware, timeout, cancellation, busy, size, read-write, wear, invalid image, and terminator codes.
Lays out upload context with a driver handle and a loader-private field.
Lays out upload operations as prepare, write, poll-complete, cancel, and cleanup callbacks operating on upload context with data buffers, offsets, sizes, and written counts.
